Benny Adam est un artiste et producteur: Benny Adam is a Moroccan-Canadian artist and producer. He has collaborated with many artists, including Niro, La Zarra, Obia le Chef, Nayra and Zach Zoya. Having produced a range of musical styles, for the past three years he has focused on a style all his own: draï, a genre that combines the rhythm of Moroccan chaâbi*, the tempo of drill and raï lyrics.
Benny Adam a ouvert son studio d’enregis: Benny Adam opened his Casablanca recording studio to La Converse. He looked back on his journey, from his teenage years in Montréal to his rediscovery of Maghrebi music, by way of his years as a producer in France.
En 2002, la sortie du film <em>8 Mile</e: In 2002, the release of the film 8 Mile inspired a number of teenagers to improvise rap battles. “Me, I’m Moroccan, I’m a wisecracker, so I was really good. With my crew, we’d go into the school bathrooms like cockroaches and rap at each other,” he recalls. One member of the crew had a computer and a headset with a microphone. That’s how they recorded their creations and passed them around on MSN. “It wasn’t like today, where everybody’s a rapper. Back then, we didn’t even think of ourselves as rappers, but just being able to hear our own voices, that was something. And me, I got bitten by the bug, because right from the start, everybody told me: ‘Wow, you’re so good!’ So I started to identify with that.”
Au Collège de Bois-de-Boulogne, il passe: At Collège de Bois-de-Boulogne, he spent more time socializing in the cafeteria than studying in the classroom. “I saw it as my first fan base. I was the rapper of Bois-de-Boulogne.” He self-produced his first album and sold about a hundred copies to his CEGEP classmates. When he started having trouble selling the rest, he organized a concert and sold the record in a bundle with tickets. “I filled the Sala Rossa at 18,” he recalls. He even managed to turn a profit and pay everyone who had helped him.
Alors qu’il pensait avoir donné le coup: Just when he thought he had launched his career, he was hit with a great disillusionment. “It was three or four years in the wilderness,” he says. “I started in music at the worst possible time. Records weren’t selling anymore. Piracy was at its peak. There was no YouTube yet, no social media. Record labels had stopped signing rappers because they didn’t believe in them anymore. And on top of that, I was in Montréal, where the hip-hop scene was practically nonexistent.”
Obstiné, Benny Adam arrête les études à: Stubborn, Benny Adam quit school at 18 and produced his own work, which he released online. “When I put out my projects, other artists would ask me who my producer was. When I told them it was me, they’d ask if I could sell them beats.” He put his career as an artist on the back burner and focused on production to earn a living. “At the start, I was the artist, I wasn’t a producer. But I can become very good at something out of necessity.”
Durant la vingtaine, alors que ses amis: In his twenties, while his friends were still living with their parents, all had cars and were travelling the world, he didn’t have enough money to visit his family in Morocco. “I was the family disgrace. They paid for my plane ticket because they wanted to see me and, obviously, I didn’t have 1,500 bucks saved up!” He even sings about it in his track Travolta : “Mom didn’t want it. Now she’s shouting: that’s my son!” “I had small jobs until I was 25, until I got my first break as a producer. And since then, that’s it, it’s all I do. It’s been my full-time job for over 10 years.”
Si, selon lui, les chances de réussite d: While he says the odds of success in music are slim, he adds that he isn’t afraid of risk. “I’m stubborn by nature. Even if people tell me it’s not possible, if I feel it in my heart, I go for it.”
Autodidacte et ingénieux, Benny Adam adm: Self-taught and resourceful, Benny Adam admits that this is his real talent. “There are plenty of people who make music as good as mine, if not better. There are plenty who write as well as I do, if not better. Where I know I have something out of the ordinary is this ability to absorb risk and to be truly stubborn.” It’s less self-confidence than a stubborn determination to see through everything he undertakes. “I’m not saying I’ll make it. I’m just saying I’ll go all the way.”
Après avoir été repéré par un producteur: After being spotted by a French producer passing through Montréal, he continued his career as a producer in Paris.
Malgré une situation précaire, il est he: Despite a precarious situation, he was happy to be playing in the big leagues. “I told myself: ‘Keep your head down and work, you’re in now. You’re not rich, you’re not comfortable, but you’re in the race.’ Before, in Montréal, I felt like I was on the sidelines, watching the NBA.” There were times when he didn’t have enough to eat. “There was a candy vending machine in the studio. The artists never took their change (20 euro cents). At the end of the day, I’d collect all the coins and buy a Kinder Bueno. And then I’d go home. Sometimes I walked for an hour when I didn’t have enough for the bus,” he recalls. “Today, I’m proud to say I got through that. But back then, I took it very hard and didn’t talk about it with anyone.”
Il se promet alors de ne pas rentrer à M: He then promised himself he wouldn’t return to Montréal without a gold record. He collected six. During this period, he co-produced rapper Niro’s album Les autres at Capitol Music France, including the hits Printemps blanc and Vamos. He notably produced tracks for rappers YL and SCH, before moving on to French pop (Tessa B., Yseult and Claudio Capéo). He is also the one who discovered La Zarra and brought her to France with him. She has enjoyed huge success: her first single, Tu t’en iras, was certified platinum in France. In Canada, the song, co-written by Benny Adam, won the International Song Award in 2023. Benny Adam shared the news on his social media, declaring himself the “first yellow-haired Moroccan to win an award at SOCAN”!
Benny Adam dans son studio d'enregistrem: Benny Adam in his recording studio in Casablanca, Morocco. (Photo: Rime El Jadidi, La Converse)
En 2022, son duo avec Amel Bent, <em>Los: In 2022, his duet with Amel Bent, Lossa, introduced him to the French public as an artist. The song has more than five million streams on Spotify to date. In Quebec, the track Start Over, with Zach Zoya, is a smash hit. It is now approaching 10 million streams on Spotify.
Sa carrière d’artiste est souvent relégu: His career as an artist is often relegated to the background. When he finds the time, he composes and produces his own tracks, which he releases on EPs titled La Barquetterie. He has put out three: in 2019, 2020 and 2021. Since 2016, his Instagram account has been named @bennyadam2024 to remind him that 2024 will be the year he releases his first album.
Malgré tout ce succès, à Paris, chaque f: Despite all this success, in Paris, every time he tried to add a touch of Maghrebi music to the work he produced, he met with flat-out rejection. That made him want to dig deeper into this path and rediscover the musical heritage of his country of origin. He started with the track Alizée, on a rhythm inspired by Visa o Passeport, a classic of Moroccan chaâbi music. Abdelaziz Stati, the performer of the original piece, even makes an appearance in the song’s music video.
<strong>Créer un genre « où Maluma pose: Creating a genre “where Maluma sings over a chaâbi beat”
Il fait des allers-retours au Maroc, ren: He travels back and forth to Morocco, meets musicians from all over the country and records instrument loops to build a bank of sound samples of Moroccan music. “For a genre to exist and flourish, it can’t be just one artist, it has to be a movement of artists. At first, I wanted to monetize this sound bank by putting it on Splice (an online platform that offers samples, loops, plugins and collaboration tools for musicians and producers). But I couldn’t be bothered, and in the meantime, I shared it with the people who came to my studio.”
Au-delà de sa carrière musicale, Benny A: Beyond his music career, Benny Adam wants to contribute to the rebirth of Maghrebi music. “I think our chaâbi rhythm can have international appeal, just like Nigerian afrobeats, just like reggaeton, just like house. My dream isn’t just to break through as an artist, it’s to create a genre where the singer Maluma sings over a chaâbi beat. [...] Today, you have artists like Tif or Dystinct who are starting to blow up with this rhythm. Where our visions differ is that I want to do only this.”
Pour lui, avoir un impact international: For him, having an international impact comes through authenticity. And it is this need for authenticity that drives him to draw on his roots and learn more about North African rhythms. “As kids in Morocco, we always heard that the Morocco of the 1970s was better, or we heard about [Morocco’s participation in] the 1986 World Cup as a historic moment for the country. Since we were only told about things we hadn’t lived through, we internalized the idea that everything Moroccan is necessarily worthless. That’s why, when you go somewhere else, even without people judging you, you feel lesser than them. I don’t want my kids to go through that. I want them to proudly say they’re Moroccan.”
Benny Adam aspire à faire de la musique: Benny Adam aspires to make music out of desire, not necessity. “I think that’s where I’d make the best music.” Until then, he has kept the promise he made to himself. His first album, titled Je t’expliquerai plus tard, is ready. It will be released in a few months.
<em>* Chaâbi : Le chaabi marocain est un: * Chaâbi: Moroccan chaabi is a lively popular music often played at celebrations. It is played with traditional instruments, such as the guembri (a three-stringed lute), derbukas (drums), lutes, as well as violins, accordion, and sometimes electric guitar for a modern touch. The word “chaâbi” means “popular” in Arabic.
En septembre 2001, Benny Adam, nouvellem: In September 2001, Benny Adam, who had just arrived in Quebec with his family, started his 2<sup>nd</sup> year of secondary school in Lachine. He still remembers the morning of September 11, and how the physics and chemistry teacher stared straight at him – the only Arab in the class – as he told the students about the terrorist attack in New York. “And then it turned into a debate in class, with all kinds of lumping together, like: ‘So do they ride around on camels in Morocco?’ I’d answer: ‘Yeah, and we stop at red lights. We’re not savages.’ I was a bit of a clown, that’s how I protected myself. I’d rather make people laugh than feel different.”
